sections.title: Two Equivalent Expressions
sections.content:
In Spanish, you have two equally natural ways to report aches:
1. **Doler**: *Me duele la cabeza* (My head hurts)
2. **Tener dolor de**: *Tengo dolor de cabeza* (I have a headache)
Both are correct and widely used by native speakers.

items.spanish: Hoy me siento mal; tengo dolor de cabeza.
items.english: Today I feel sick; I have a headache.

items.spanish: Me duele la espalda después de trabajar sentado.
items.english: My back hurts after working sitting down.

items.spanish: ¿Tienes dolor de muelas? Debes ir al dentista.
items.english: Do you have a toothache? You should go to the dentist.

sections.content: Notice that with *tener*, you say *dolor de cabeza* (no article after *de*). With *doler*, you keep the article: *me duele **la** cabeza*.
